Summary: Provision the DigitalOcean App Platform environment
User Story: As a developer, I want the backend and frontend deployed as components of one App Platform application, so that requests stay same-origin and there is one place to configure the deployment.
Why: Requests stay same-origin and there is one place to configure the deployment
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a push to the staging branch, when CI passes, then the app builds and deploys automatically | 2. Given the frontend and backend are separate components, when a browser calls the API, then no CORS preflight is required | 3. Environment variables are set per environment and no secret appears in the repository

Summary: Provision Managed PostgreSQL with connection pooling
User Story: As a developer, I want a managed database with a transaction-mode connection pool, so that the application does not exhaust the connection limit and RLS context works correctly.
Why: The application does not exhaust the connection limit and RLS context works correctly
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Prisma connects through the DigitalOcean connection pool | 2. Given the pool is in transaction mode, when set_config is called with the transaction-local flag, then the tenant context persists for that transaction only | 3. Point-in-time recovery is enabled and confirmed in the control panel

Summary: Create separate public and private Spaces buckets
User Story: As a compliance owner, I want listing images public and identity documents private, so that a customer identity document is never reachable from a guessable URL.
Why: A customer identity document is never reachable from a guessable URL
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Listing images are served from a public bucket via CDN | 2. Given an identity document is uploaded, when its URL is requested without a signature, then access is denied | 3. Given a verified staff member requests a document, when the API responds, then it returns a presigned URL expiring in 15 minutes

Summary: Set up the CI pipeline with a real PostgreSQL service
User Story: As a developer, I want lint, unit and integration tests to run on every pull request against a real database, so that database-level guarantees such as constraints and RLS are actually exercised.
Why: Database-level guarantees such as constraints and RLS are actually exercised
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a pull request is opened, when CI runs, then lint, unit and integration tests all execute | 2. Integration tests connect as the application role, never as a database superuser | 3. Given any test fails, when the pull request is reviewed, then merging is blocked

User Story: As a frontend developer, I want an agreed OpenAPI definition of the core endpoints, so that I can build screens against a contract instead of waiting for the backend to finish.
Why: I can build screens against a contract instead of waiting for the backend to finish
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Core booking, listing, payment, auth and operator endpoints are defined with request and response shapes | 2. The unified error shape from 6.6.2 is defined once and referenced by every endpoint | 3. The contract is published to the team repository before Phase 1 work begins

Summary: Create the module skeleton and dependency lint rule
User Story: As a developer, I want folders that reflect module ownership and a lint rule that enforces the boundary, so that cross-module table access is caught by the build rather than by review.
Why: Cross-module table access is caught by the build rather than by review
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Each of the twelve modules has its own folder with route, service and data-access layers | 2. Given a module imports the raw Prisma client outside the allowlist, when CI runs, then the build fails | 3. Given a module queries a table it does not own, when the conformance script runs, then the build fails

User Story: As a developer, I want a wrapped client exposing withOperatorContext only, so that the tenant context can never be forgotten on a tenant-scoped query.
Why: The tenant context can never be forgotten on a tenant-scoped query
Acceptance Criteria: 1. withOperatorContext opens a transaction, sets the tenant context and commits | 2. Given a query runs with no tenant context, when RLS policies are active, then zero rows are returned rather than all rows | 3. The raw client is not exported from the shared database module

Summary: Implement the job queue and worker
User Story: As a developer, I want a Postgres-backed job queue with lease-based claiming, so that background work survives restarts and is never silently lost.
Why: Background work survives restarts and is never silently lost
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Jobs are claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a five-minute lease | 2. Given the worker is killed mid-job, when the lease expires, then the job is reclaimed and completed exactly once | 3. Given a job fails five times, when it exhausts retries, then it moves to failed and appears in the admin queue | 4. The worker runs from its own entry point in the same codebase

User Story: As a product owner, I want features toggled per environment and per operator, so that incomplete work can be merged without appearing in a demonstration.
Why: Incomplete work can be merged without appearing in a demonstration
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Flags are read from the database and cached in memory with a short refresh | 2. Given a flag is disabled, when a customer loads the page, then neither the API route nor the UI element is available | 3. Flags can be scoped to a single operator

User Story: As a developer, I want the full schema with constraints, indexes and enums, so that integrity is enforced by the database rather than by application code.
Why: Integrity is enforced by the database rather than by application code
Acceptance Criteria: 1. All tables from Section 5.3 exist with the stated primary keys and constraints | 2. The composite foreign key from payments to payment_schedules is present | 3. The documents CHECK constraint permits exactly one owner | 4. listing_availability has its composite primary key and non-negative check

Summary: Write incremental migration and data backfill scripts
User Story: As a developer, I want historical data migrated without loss, so that the existing system's bookings and payments survive the refactor.
Why: The existing system's bookings and payments survive the refactor
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Operator entities are created from existing operator profiles | 2. Given a historical booking with dates in booking_details, when the backfill runs, then service_start_at and service_end_at are populated | 3. Given a booking whose dates cannot be parsed, when the backfill runs, then it is written to an exception table rather than guessed | 4. Payment schedules are generated from existing deadlines and deposit values

Summary: Rehearse the migration against a production-sized snapshot
User Story: As a team lead, I want evidence that the migration is safe and a known cutover duration, so that we are not discovering migration problems during go-live.
Why: We are not discovering migration problems during go-live
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Row counts per table before and after match or the difference is explained | 2. Referential integrity passes after constraints are applied | 3. Execution time is recorded and establishes the cutover window | 4. The count of unparseable bookings is recorded and is a release gate

Summary: Generate availability rows on a rolling horizon
User Story: As a operator, I want availability rows created automatically for future dates, so that I do not have to configure every future date by hand.
Why: I do not have to configure every future date by hand
Acceptance Criteria: 1. A nightly job extends availability 180 days forward from the listing default daily quantity | 2. Given a date has no availability row, when a customer tries to book it, then it is treated as unavailable | 3. Given an operator has blocked a date, when the horizon job runs, then the block is preserved

Summary: Add idempotency to booking and payment endpoints
User Story: As a customer, I want a repeated submission not to create a second booking, so that a slow network or a double tap does not cost me twice.
Why: A slow network or a double tap does not cost me twice
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given the same idempotency key is submitted twice, when the second request arrives, then the original response is returned | 2. Idempotency records expire automatically after 24 hours | 3. Given no key is supplied on a write endpoint, when the request arrives, then it is rejected with a clear error

User Story: As a platform, I want payment callbacks verified, persisted and processed asynchronously, so that no payment is lost and no event is processed twice.
Why: No payment is lost and no event is processed twice
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Signature is verified against the raw request body before any parsing | 2. Given a duplicate event id, when it is received, then the unique constraint prevents reprocessing and 200 is returned | 3. The endpoint returns 200 before business processing occurs | 4. Given the worker processes the event, when it completes, then the payment schedule is marked paid

User Story: As a finance owner, I want pending payments checked against the gateway, so that a lost callback does not leave a paid booking marked unpaid.
Why: A lost callback does not leave a paid booking marked unpaid
Acceptance Criteria: 1. A scheduled job polls payments approaching their due date and queries Stripe directly | 2. Given the gateway reports paid but the local record does not, when the sweep runs, then the local record is corrected and logged | 3. Every correction is written to the audit log

Summary: Make scheduled tasks safe and observable
User Story: As a operator, I want scheduled jobs that run exactly once and log their outcome, so that expired bookings are never cancelled twice or missed entirely.
Why: Expired bookings are never cancelled twice or missed entirely
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Every job acquires a Postgres advisory lock before running | 2. Given two instances start the same job, when the lock is held, then only one executes | 3. Each run writes name, start, end, processed count, failure count and errors to cron_job_logs | 4. A daily sweep catches anything the primary job missed

User Story: As a administrator, I want every sensitive action recorded with before and after values, so that data changes can be traced and responsibility established.
Why: Data changes can be traced and responsibility established
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Forced status changes, configuration changes, refunds, tier overrides and promotion overrides are all logged | 2. Each record captures actor, action, entity, before, after, IP address and timestamp | 3. Audit records cannot be updated or deleted through the API

Summary: Implement the unified error contract and request tracing
User Story: As a frontend developer, I want a consistent error shape with a request identifier, so that I can branch on a code and trace an error back to a server log.
Why: I can branch on a code and trace an error back to a server log
Acceptance Criteria: 1. All errors return code, message, request_id and optional details | 2. Given an error occurs, when it is logged, then the same request_id appears in the log and in the error tracker | 3. Clients never need to match on message text

Summary: Model operator organisations and staff membership
User Story: As a operator manager, I want multiple staff accounts under my company, so that my counter staff can process bookings without sharing my login.
Why: My counter staff can process bookings without sharing my login
Acceptance Criteria: 1. An operator organisation exists independently of any user account | 2. Given a manager invites a staff member, when they accept, then they can access only that operator's data | 3. Given a person is both a customer and operator staff, when they log in, then both identities work

Summary: Implement the token lifecycle with immediate revocation
User Story: As a administrator, I want a disabled account to stop working immediately, so that suspending an operator actually suspends them.
Why: Suspending an operator actually suspends them
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Access tokens last 60 minutes; refresh tokens last 7 days and are stored in the database | 2. Given an account is disabled, when its next request arrives, then it is rejected without waiting for token expiry | 3. Given a consumed refresh token is reused, when it is presented, then the whole token family is revoked

Summary: Apply row-level security policies and prove isolation
User Story: As a platform, I want tenant isolation enforced by the database, so that a coding mistake cannot expose one operator's data to another.
Why: A coding mistake cannot expose one operator's data to another
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Policies are applied to every tenant-scoped table | 2. Given operator A calls the API for operator B's bookings, when the request is handled, then 403 is returned | 3. Given the Prisma middleware is bypassed and the tenant context is set to A, when B's rows are queried directly, then zero rows return | 4. Given no tenant context is set, when a query runs, then zero rows return

User Story: As a customer, I want my account protected against password guessing, so that someone cannot brute force their way into my bookings.
Why: Someone cannot brute force their way into my bookings
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Five consecutive failures lock the account for 15 minutes | 2. Unlocking requires email verification | 3. Password length and complexity are enforced at registration and change

User Story: As a operator, I want to connect my bank account so I get paid, so that money from my bookings reaches me automatically.
Why: Money from my bookings reaches me automatically
Acceptance Criteria: 1. An operator can start Stripe Express onboarding from the back office | 2. Given onboarding is incomplete, when the operator views the dashboard, then the outstanding steps are shown | 3. Given onboarding completes, when Stripe confirms, then onboarding_status is updated via webhook

Summary: Write the commission ledger with both funding formulas
User Story: As a platform, I want commission calculated correctly for operator-funded and platform-funded discounts, so that the ledger reconciles against Stripe line by line.
Why: The ledger reconciles against Stripe line by line
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given an operator-funded discount, when a payment succeeds, then fee_amount equals net_amount times fee_rate | 2. Given a platform-funded discount, when a payment succeeds, then the operator receives gross less commission and the platform margin may be negative | 3. fee_rate and funded_by are snapshotted onto the ledger entry at payment time | 4. stripe_fee_amount is stored separately and never folded into fee_amount | 5. All amounts are stored as integer sen

Summary: Generate payouts for settleable bookings only
User Story: As a operator, I want to be paid after the service is delivered, so that the platform is not exposed to chargebacks on money it has already released.
Why: The platform is not exposed to chargebacks on money it has already released
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Only ledger entries whose booking reached completed or no_show and passed the appeal window are included | 2. Given a booking is refunded before payout, when the payout runs, then that entry is excluded | 3. A ledger entry can never appear in two payouts | 4. The payout job runs under the system database role, not a tenant context

User Story: As a operator, I want to see how each booking became my payout, so that I can verify the platform's arithmetic myself.
Why: I can verify the platform's arithmetic myself
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Each line shows gross, discount, who funded it, commission, processing fee and net | 2. Payouts list their constituent bookings | 3. The report can be exported as CSV

Summary: Compute credit profiles and resolve tiers
User Story: As a platform, I want a customer's credit tier derived from their history, so that payment terms reflect actual reliability.
Why: Payment terms reflect actual reliability
Acceptance Criteria: 1. A new customer defaults to Normal | 2. Given three successful on-time payments and no expiries, when recomputation runs, then the customer becomes Trusted | 3. Given two expired bookings, when recomputation runs, then the customer becomes Caution | 4. Counters are maintained incrementally from events, never by scanning the bookings table

Summary: Generate payment schedules from the credit tier
User Story: As a customer, I want payment terms that match my standing, so that I know exactly what is due and when.
Why: I know exactly what is due and when
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a Normal customer, when a booking is created, then one schedule entry is due in 24 hours | 2. Given a Caution customer, when a booking is created, then a 30 percent deposit is due in 12 hours and a 70 percent balance 24 hours before service start | 3. Given a High Risk customer, when a booking is created, then full prepayment is required immediately | 4. Given a booking reaches a terminal state, when it does, then outstanding entries are voided rather than deleted

User Story: As a operator, I want a limit on how many unpaid bookings one customer can hold, so that a new account cannot occupy my inventory across many bookings at once.
Why: A new account cannot occupy my inventory across many bookings at once
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Limits are Normal 2, Trusted 5, Caution 1, High Risk 0, read from system settings | 2. The count runs inside the same transaction as the inventory reservation | 3. Given a Normal customer with two open unpaid bookings submits three more concurrently, when they are processed, then all three are refused | 4. A refusal returns a clear message and does not create a negative credit event

Summary: Implement no-show marking and terminal outcomes
User Story: As a operator staff, I want to mark a customer as not appeared, so that I am compensated for inventory I held and the customer's record reflects it.
Why: I am compensated for inventory I held and the customer's record reflects it
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Marking is only possible between service start and the end of no_show_window_hours | 2. A remark is mandatory | 3. Given a fully paid booking, when marked, then status is no_show, inventory is not released and the full net becomes settleable after the appeal window | 4. Given a deposit-paid booking with an unpaid balance, when marked, then status is no_show_unpaid, outstanding entries are voided, the deposit is forfeited to the operator and only the deposit becomes settleable

Summary: Record credit events and support appeals
User Story: As a customer, I want to see why my tier changed and to dispute it, so that a mistaken no-show does not permanently damage my standing.
Why: A mistaken no-show does not permanently damage my standing
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Every tier change writes an event with reason, actor and before and after tiers | 2. Given a customer appeals, when an administrator upholds it, then a reversing event is written and the tier is recomputed | 3. The original event is never modified or deleted | 4. The customer can view their own credit history

User Story: As a operator, I want unpaid bookings cancelled automatically at their deadline, so that my inventory is released rather than held indefinitely.
Why: My inventory is released rather than held indefinitely
Acceptance Criteria: 1. The job works from payment_schedules due dates, in Malaysia time | 2. Given a schedule entry passes its due date unpaid, when the sweep runs, then the booking expires, inventory is released and the customer is notified | 3. Given the job runs twice, when the advisory lock is held, then no booking is cancelled twice

Summary: Create and manage car rental listings
User Story: As a operator staff, I want to publish a vehicle with its specifications and rules, so that customers can find and understand what they are booking.
Why: Customers can find and understand what they are booking
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Vehicle type, seats, transmission, luggage capacity and description are structured fields | 2. Pickup and return rules and insurance notes are captured | 3. Given a listing is incomplete, when publishing is attempted, then the missing required fields are named | 4. Given a listing is unpublished, when a customer searches, then it does not appear

Summary: Create and manage tour package listings
User Story: As a operator staff, I want to publish a tour with its itinerary and inclusions, so that customers understand what the package covers before booking.
Why: Customers understand what the package covers before booking
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Duration, highlights, daily itinerary, inclusions, exclusions, meeting point and maximum group size are captured | 2. Given a tour has a maximum group size, when a customer books more places than remain, then the booking is refused

User Story: As a operator staff, I want to upload photographs and choose the main one, so that my listing looks credible to a customer who has never heard of my company.
Why: My listing looks credible to a customer who has never heard of my company
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Multiple images upload to the public Spaces bucket | 2. Images can be reordered and one set as primary | 3. Given a file exceeds the size limit or is not an image, when uploaded, then it is rejected with a clear message

User Story: As a operator, I want weekend, holiday and seasonal pricing, so that I can charge what the market bears without editing every listing daily.
Why: I can charge what the market bears without editing every listing daily
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Rules support date range and weekday mask, with fixed or percentage adjustment | 2. Given multiple rules apply, when price is calculated, then they combine by priority | 3. Given a date range is selected, when the operator previews, then the resulting nightly prices are shown | 4. The same calculation runs server side at booking time; the client never supplies the price

User Story: As a operator staff, I want to offer extras such as a child seat or airport transfer, so that I can increase revenue per booking.
Why: I can increase revenue per booking
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Add-ons carry a name, description and unit price | 2. Given a customer selects add-ons, when the total is computed, then add-ons are included in gross_amount and therefore in the commission base

Summary: Manage locations and link them to listings
User Story: As a operator, I want a library of pickup and meeting points reused across listings, so that I do not retype the same address on every listing.
Why: I do not retype the same address on every listing
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Locations carry name, address, coordinates and type | 2. A listing can be linked to several locations with a role of pickup, dropoff or meeting point | 3. Given a customer books, when they choose a pickup point, then it is stored on the booking

User Story: As a customer, I want to filter by the things I actually care about, so that I can find a seven-seat automatic in Kuching without scrolling through everything.
Why: I can find a seven-seat automatic in Kuching without scrolling through everything
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Full-text search across title, description and destination using tsvector with a GIN index | 2. Car filters: vehicle type, price range, seats, transmission, pickup location, operator | 3. Tour filters: destination, duration, departure date, price range, group size | 4. Given dates are supplied, when results are returned, then only listings with availability across the whole range appear

User Story: As a operator, I want tiered refund rules by how far ahead the customer cancels, so that refund amounts are calculated rather than argued about.
Why: Refund amounts are calculated rather than argued about
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Policies define hours before service and refund percentage, with priority | 2. Resolution order is listing, then operator, then system default | 3. Given a customer cancels, when the refund is computed, then the applicable tier is shown with the amount

User Story: As a operator staff, I want to set how many units are sellable each day and block dates, so that I do not accept bookings for vehicles that are already out.
Why: I do not accept bookings for vehicles that are already out
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Daily quantity can be set for a listing across a date range | 2. A date can be blocked without deleting its row | 3. Given a date is blocked, when a customer searches, then it is unavailable

User Story: As a platform, I want a multi-day booking to reserve every day or none, so that two customers can never be sold the same vehicle for overlapping dates.
Why: Two customers can never be sold the same vehicle for overlapping dates
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Reservation is a single ranged UPDATE with a row-count assertion | 2. Given the affected row count is fewer than the number of days, when the check runs, then the transaction rolls back and the booking is refused | 3. Given a date has no availability row, when reservation is attempted, then it is treated as unavailable | 4. Reservation runs in the same transaction as the exposure check and the booking insert

Summary: Release inventory on cancellation and expiry
User Story: As a operator, I want inventory returned when a booking falls through, so that a lapsed booking does not block a real one.
Why: A lapsed booking does not block a real one
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Cancellation, expiry, rejection and refusal release the quantity across the same date range | 2. Given a booking is marked no_show, when it terminates, then inventory is not released | 3. Release is idempotent so a repeated event does not over-credit inventory

User Story: As a team lead, I want test evidence that the inventory guarantee holds, so that we can defend the claim at the project viva.
Why: We can defend the claim at the project viva
Acceptance Criteria: 1. 50 concurrent bookings against one remaining unit produce exactly one success | 2. Two overlapping five-day bookings against one unit produce exactly one success with no partial reservation | 3. 30 concurrent overlapping bookings complete with no deadlock | 4. Results are captured as a report artefact

User Story: As a customer, I want to complete a booking in one step, so that I get a confirmed booking and a clear payment schedule.
Why: I get a confirmed booking and a clear payment schedule
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Price, promotion and tier lookups happen before the transaction opens | 2. Exposure check, inventory reservation, booking insert, schedule creation and notification enqueue are one transaction | 3. Given any step fails, when the transaction rolls back, then no inventory is held and no booking exists | 4. The response returns the booking reference and the full payment schedule

User Story: As a operator, I want bookings that move through defined states with a full history, so that disputes can be resolved by looking at the record.
Why: Disputes can be resolved by looking at the record
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Every transition writes a history record with actor, old state, new state and remark | 2. Invalid transitions are rejected | 3. Terminal states are completed, cancelled, expired, no_show, no_show_unpaid and rejected

User Story: As a customer, I want to cancel and know what I get back, so that I am not surprised by the refund amount.
Why: I am not surprised by the refund amount
Acceptance Criteria: 1. The applicable cancellation policy tier is resolved and the refund amount shown before confirming | 2. Given a refund is issued, when it is processed, then a refund record is created and the commission ledger is adjusted | 3. Partial and repeated refunds against one payment are supported

User Story: As a operator staff, I want to accept, reject or propose an alternative, individually or in bulk, so that I can clear a morning's bookings quickly.
Why: I can clear a morning's bookings quickly
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Bookings can be accepted or rejected with an optional note | 2. Given several bookings are selected, when a bulk action is applied, then each is processed independently and failures are reported per booking | 3. Rejection releases inventory and notifies the customer

User Story: As a customer, I want to apply a discount code at checkout, so that I benefit from a campaign I was sent.
Why: I benefit from a campaign I was sent
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Code validity, date window, minimum spend and usage limit are checked at booking time | 2. A redemption record is created inside the booking transaction, one per booking | 3. Given a platform-funded code, when the ledger is written, then the operator is made whole and the platform absorbs the discount

User Story: As a marketing owner, I want to know which channel produced a booking, so that we can tell what marketing spend actually worked.
Why: We can tell what marketing spend actually worked
Acceptance Criteria: 1. UTM source, medium and campaign are captured on the booking when present | 2. Channel is recorded as web, mobile or WhatsApp | 3. Attribution is queryable in the admin reporting view

User Story: As a customer, I want instant answers to common questions, so that I do not wait for a human to tell me my payment deadline.
Why: I do not wait for a human to tell me my payment deadline
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Quick action menu covers booking status, payment schedule, cancellation policy, credit tier and receipt upload | 2. Given a question matches a rule, when it is handled, then no LLM call is made | 3. Rule responses are configurable without a code change

Summary: Add the LLM fallback with a circuit breaker
User Story: As a customer, I want a useful answer to a question the rules do not cover, so that I am not stuck when my question is slightly unusual.
Why: I am not stuck when my question is slightly unusual
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Claude is called with only the signed-in user's own booking context, enforced at the query layer | 2. Given the call exceeds 5 seconds, when it times out, then the rule engine responds instead | 3. Given ten consecutive failures, when the circuit opens, then no LLM calls are made for 10 minutes | 4. No identity document content is ever sent to the model

Summary: Persist conversations and escalate to a human
User Story: As a operator staff, I want to see and answer customer questions the bot could not handle, so that a customer problem does not disappear.
Why: A customer problem does not disappear
Acceptance Criteria: 1. All messages are persisted with read state | 2. Given the bot cannot resolve a question, when it escalates, then a ticket is created and the operator is notified | 3. The operator can reply from the back office and the customer sees it

User Story: As a customer, I want to register, sign in and manage my details, so that I can use the platform and keep my information current.
Why: I can use the platform and keep my information current
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Register, sign in, forgot password and change password all work | 2. Consent to the privacy policy and terms is captured with timestamp and IP at registration | 3. Identity documents upload to the private bucket and show verification status

Summary: Build the home page and search entry
User Story: As a customer, I want to start a search from the first screen, so that I can find what I need without learning the site.
Why: I can find what I need without learning the site
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Search bar covers business type, destination or pickup point, dates and party size | 2. Category entry points for car rental and tours | 3. Featured listings render from seeded content while content management is deferred

User Story: As a customer, I want to narrow results to what suits me, so that I do not have to open twenty listings to compare.
Why: I do not have to open twenty listings to compare
Acceptance Criteria: 1. All filters from BNPL-040 are available and combine | 2. Sorting by price, newest and popularity works; rating sort appears only when the review flag is on | 3. Given no results, when the page renders, then it suggests relaxing a filter rather than showing a blank page

User Story: As a customer, I want to see everything about a package before I commit, so that I know what is included and what happens if I cancel.
Why: I know what is included and what happens if I cancel
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Image carousel, specifications, itinerary, pricing rules, cancellation policy and operator information all render | 2. Add-ons are selectable and update the displayed total | 3. The review section renders only when the review display flag is enabled

Summary: Build the booking and payment flow
User Story: As a customer, I want to book and pay with the terms shown clearly, so that I am never surprised by a second deadline.
Why: I am never surprised by a second deadline
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Date and party selection, add-ons, contact details, summary and terms acceptance | 2. The full payment schedule with every due date and a countdown is shown before submission | 3. The customer's credit tier and what it means is explained on the payment page | 4. Given the exposure cap is reached, when the customer opens the flow, then this is explained before they fill the form

User Story: As a customer, I want to see my bookings, payments and credit record, so that I can manage what I have booked and understand my standing.
Why: I can manage what I have booked and understand my standing
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Bookings list with status filter and detail view | 2. Cancellation request and no-show appeal entry points | 3. Credit record shows current tier and the reason for each change | 4. Notification centre and receipt download

User Story: As a operator manager, I want today's numbers at a glance, so that I know what needs attention this morning.
Why: I know what needs attention this morning
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Cards for pending bookings, confirmed today, revenue today and month-to-date volume | 2. Seven day volume and revenue trend | 3. Shortcut links to pending actions

Summary: Build order management with no-show marking
User Story: As a operator staff, I want to process bookings and record no-shows, so that my day's work happens in one screen.
Why: My day's work happens in one screen
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Filterable list, detail view, accept, reject and bulk actions | 2. Given a booking is within its no-show window, when staff mark it, then a remark is required and the outcome matrix is applied | 3. Given the window has closed, when marking is attempted, then the action is unavailable with an explanation | 4. Internal notes are visible to operator staff only

User Story: As a operator staff, I want to create and edit my listings, so that I can get my inventory onto the platform.
Why: I can get my inventory onto the platform
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Create, edit, publish and unpublish for both listing types | 2. Image upload with reordering | 3. Add-on and location assignment

User Story: As a operator staff, I want to see and adjust availability by day, so that I can block a day when a vehicle goes for service.
Why: I can block a day when a vehicle goes for service
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Calendar shows bookings and remaining quantity per day | 2. Dates can be blocked and daily quantity adjusted directly | 3. Given a date is beyond the generated horizon, when it renders, then it shows as not yet open rather than unavailable

User Story: As a operator, I want to set up seasonal and weekend pricing visually, so that I do not need a developer to change my rates.
Why: I do not need a developer to change my rates
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Base price, weekend, holiday and seasonal rules can be created and edited | 2. Given a date range is selected, when preview runs, then the resulting daily prices are displayed | 3. Rules can be applied to several listings at once

User Story: As a operator manager, I want to configure my trading rules, so that the platform reflects how my business actually works.
Why: The platform reflects how my business actually works
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Payment deadline, deposit percentage and no-show window are configurable | 2. Cancellation policy tiers can be created and edited | 3. Location library management | 4. Notification preferences

User Story: As a administrator, I want platform-wide health at a glance, so that I can spot a problem before an operator reports it.
Why: I can spot a problem before an operator reports it
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Total bookings, revenue, active operators and registered users | 2. Seven day trends | 3. Alerts for payment failure rate, callback backlog and scheduled task failures

User Story: As a administrator, I want to review, approve, suspend and support operators, so that only legitimate businesses trade on the platform.
Why: Only legitimate businesses trade on the platform
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Registration review queue with business licence document viewing | 2. Approve, suspend and reactivate with reason, all audit logged | 3. Given an operator is suspended, when their staff make a request, then it is refused immediately | 4. Operator staff accounts are visible and can be reset

User Story: As a administrator, I want to intervene on a problem booking, so that a stuck booking can be resolved without database access.
Why: A stuck booking can be resolved without database access
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Platform-wide search and filter across operators | 2. Forced status change and forced cancellation with mandatory reason | 3. Every intervention is written to the audit log

Summary: Build the credit appeal review queue
User Story: As a administrator, I want to decide customer appeals against no-show marks, so that a customer wrongly marked is not permanently penalised.
Why: A customer wrongly marked is not permanently penalised
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Queue shows the disputed event, related booking, operator remark and customer statement | 2. Given an appeal is upheld, when it is saved, then a reversing event is written and the tier recomputed | 3. Given an appeal is rejected, when it is saved, then the decision and reason are recorded | 4. Both outcomes write to the audit log

User Story: As a marketing owner, I want to create campaigns and see how they performed, so that we can run promotions without engineering help.
Why: We can run promotions without engineering help
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Codes with type, value, minimum spend, validity window and usage limits | 2. Platform or operator funding is selected explicitly | 3. Given a platform-funded discount exceeds the commission, when saving, then it is rejected unless explicitly overridden and the projected margin impact is shown | 4. Redemption and attribution reporting

Summary: Build system settings and feature flag management
User Story: As a administrator, I want to change platform rules without a deployment, so that we can tune the platform during the pilot.
Why: We can tune the platform during the pilot
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Commission rate, default payment deadline, credit tier thresholds and exposure limits are editable | 2. Feature flags can be toggled globally or per operator | 3. Every change is audit logged with before and after values

Summary: Add error tracking and structured logging
User Story: As a developer, I want exceptions captured with stack traces and correlated logs, so that I can diagnose a production problem without a customer describing it.
Why: I can diagnose a production problem without a customer describing it
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Sentry or equivalent captures frontend and backend exceptions | 2. Logs are structured and carry the request identifier | 3. Alert rules fire on error rate spikes | 4. Payment, booking and settlement logs are retained permanently

User Story: As a product owner, I want key user actions recorded as events, so that we can measure whether the pilot worked instead of guessing.
Why: We can measure whether the pilot worked instead of guessing
Acceptance Criteria: 1. An analytics_events table stores event name, user, operator, booking, properties and timestamp | 2. Events emitted: search_performed, listing_viewed, booking_started, booking_created, payment_succeeded, payment_expired, booking_completed, no_show_marked, exposure_blocked, chat_escalated | 3. Credit tier is recorded on the booking_created event so tier outcomes can be compared later | 4. Emission happens through the job queue and never blocks the user request

User Story: As a product owner, I want a single admin screen showing the pilot scorecard, so that we can run a weekly review without writing SQL.
Why: We can run a weekly review without writing SQL
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Shows bookings created, paid, completed, expired and no-show counts for a selected period | 2. Shows on-time payment rate and expiry rate broken down by credit tier | 3. Shows GMV, commission revenue and settled payout totals | 4. Figures can be exported as CSV for the project report

Summary: Publish terms of service and privacy policy
User Story: As a platform, I want real legal text published before any customer registers, so that we are not collecting personal data without a lawful basis.
Why: We are not collecting personal data without a lawful basis
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Privacy policy covers what is collected, why, retention and PDPA rights | 2. Terms of service cover booking, deferred payment, no-show forfeiture and cancellation | 3. Both are linked at registration and consent is recorded | 4. Reviewed by the client before publication

Summary: Build the operator onboarding kit and bulk listing import
User Story: As a operator, I want to get my fleet onto the platform without hours of typing, so that the platform is worth joining.
Why: The platform is worth joining
Acceptance Criteria: 1. A CSV template covering listings, base price and default daily quantity | 2. Given a valid CSV is uploaded, when it is processed, then listings and availability rows are created and a summary is shown | 3. Given a row is invalid, when import runs, then that row is reported with the reason and the rest still import | 4. A short written guide for operator staff covering listing, pricing and order handling

Summary: Complete Stripe live mode and operator KYC
User Story: As a platform, I want live payment processing with connected operator accounts, so that the pilot can move real money.
Why: The pilot can move real money
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Platform account activated for live mode | 2. Each pilot operator completes Stripe Express onboarding and reaches payouts-enabled | 3. One live low-value end-to-end test booking is completed and settled per operator | 4. Refund tested end to end in live mode

User Story: As a client, I want clarity on who issues the invoice and what the platform must file, so that the pilot does not create a tax liability nobody planned for.
Why: The pilot does not create a tax liability nobody planned for
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Determine whether the platform or the operator is the invoicing party for a booking | 2. Confirm current Malaysian e-invoicing obligations for both parties with a qualified adviser | 3. Decide whether invoices generated by the platform satisfy those obligations for the pilot | 4. Record the decision and any required follow-up work

Summary: Define the support model for the pilot
User Story: As a pilot customer, I want someone to answer when something goes wrong, so that a failed payment does not become an abandoned customer.
Why: A failed payment does not become an abandoned customer
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Named person on rota for customer and operator escalations during the pilot | 2. Response target agreed with the client and communicated to operators | 3. Escalation path for payment failures, disputed no-shows and settlement queries | 4. A short runbook covering the five most likely failures

User Story: As a client, I want two to three operators live with real listings, so that the pilot has supply before it seeks demand.
Why: The pilot has supply before it seeks demand
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Two to three operators identified, agreed and contracted with the client | 2. Each has at least five published listings with pricing and 60 days of availability | 3. Each has completed a training walkthrough of order handling and no-show marking | 4. Each has confirmed their bank details are connected and payouts are enabled

Summary: Run the go-live checklist and cutover
User Story: As a team lead, I want a controlled production release with a rollback path, so that go-live is an event we planned rather than survived.
Why: Go-live is an event we planned rather than survived
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Migration executed within the rehearsed window | 2. Smoke test covering registration, search, booking, payment, settlement and refund | 3. Monitoring and alerting confirmed active | 4. The frozen Vercel deployment remains available as a fallback until acceptance is signed off

Summary: Enable review submission and operator replies
User Story: As a customer, I want to review a trip I completed, so that other customers can trust an operator they have not used.
Why: Other customers can trust an operator they have not used
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Only bookings in completed status can be reviewed, one review each | 2. Operators can reply once per review | 3. Enabling the display flag surfaces ratings on detail pages and rating sort in search

Summary: Add favourites and price drop alerts
User Story: As a customer, I want to save listings and be told when they get cheaper, so that I can wait for a better price instead of forgetting the listing.
Why: I can wait for a better price instead of forgetting the listing
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Listings can be saved and appear in the personal centre | 2. Given a saved listing's price falls, when the check runs, then the customer is notified once

User Story: As a customer, I want to book from my phone, so that I can book while travelling without a laptop.
Why: I can book while travelling without a laptop
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Home, search, detail, booking, payment, my bookings and push notifications | 2. Receipt photo upload for DuitNow | 3. Built against the /v1 API with no mobile-specific backend

User Story: As a customer, I want to book through WhatsApp, so that I can use the channel I already have open.
Why: I can use the channel I already have open
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Signature verified on every inbound webhook | 2. Given an unverified phone number, when it is used, then only browse, create and pay for that session are permitted | 3. Given a customer verifies via one-time code, when verification completes, then the identity is linked and marked verified | 4. Status updates and payment links are delivered through approved templates

User Story: As a operator, I want suggestions on when to raise or lower prices, so that I can price to demand without studying the data myself.
Why: I can price to demand without studying the data myself
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Forecast runs against real booking history | 2. Given an operator has fewer bookings than the minimum threshold, when the dashboard loads, then the module shows as awaiting data | 3. Suggestions are advisory and never change a price automatically

User Story: As a marketing owner, I want to manage the carousel, featured placements and announcements, so that we can promote campaigns without a deployment.
Why: We can promote campaigns without a deployment
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Carousel images and links are manageable | 2. Featured listing placements are configurable | 3. Announcements can be published with a validity window
